cohort: 5236 women who gave birth at the University Hospital 'Federico II' of Naples, Italy, between 2020 and 2021
finding: Women who tested positive for SARS-CoV-2 at the time of labor had 80% increased odds of caesarean section compared to those who tested negative, after adjusting for the SARS-CoV-2 variant.
mod_finding: Women who tested positive for SARS-CoV-2 at the time of labor had 80% increased odds of caesarean section compared to those who tested negative, after adjusting for the SARS-CoV-2 variant.
